$comment: YOFO Review's own contract (ADR 0014, plan 2026-10-01-standalone-review-app): the review bridge (crates/mib-bridge/src/review_bridge.rs, review_shim.cpp) and the YOFO Review shell. Separate from bridge-contract.json, the MIB Studio backend bridge ABI, which it never changes. C++ ties to these values via static_asserts in review_shim.cpp; Rust via tests/review_bridge.rs; TypeScript via the generated desktop/src/review/reviewContract.ts and desktop/src-tauri/src/review_packet_contract.rs (scripts/gen_bridge_contract.py --check fails CI on drift). Additive changes only: append values, never renumber or repurpose.

run_identity.source: run snapshot v3 (#712, /run_provenance @run_snapshot_json) and the planned annotation (/experiment_annotation @annotation_json, @annotation_schema_version); fetch_review_info.identity for the open file, review_probe_runs per file (review ABI 2, #717 B1a; emodulus_lut and profile_id since review ABI 3, #717 B3b; since review ABI 5, #783, emodulus_lut also reads a regenerated file's /experiment_info @emodulus_lut_json, named by emodulus_lut_provenance)
run_identity.members: snapshot_version, run_id, experiment_id, run_index, sample_ref, calibration_record_id, operator (id, name), annotation (sample, condition, experimental_unit, concentration {value, unit}, channel, medium, temperature_c, notes, free key/values sorted by key, schema_version), emodulus_lut (loaded, lut_id, revision, source, sha256, catalog_sha256, checksum_status: the snapshot v3 record, else a regenerated file's @emodulus_lut_json; the snapshot record wins, as in recording::readFileEModulusLut), emodulus_lut_provenance (review ABI 5, #783: one of emodulus_lut_provenances; snapshot = the run snapshot v3 record, the run's own; recorded = a regenerated file's record carried over from its source run; host = a regenerated file's record of the host's E-LUT at regeneration, the source recording none; absent exactly when emodulus_lut is), profile_id (the snapshot's profile_id, a non-empty string)
run_identity.absent_semantics: a member the file does not record is absent: has_* false over the review bridge, null in the shell's JSON; never 0, false or an empty string. A legacy file without a snapshot has has_snapshot false and every member absent, except that a file regenerated from #764 on (no snapshot) carries emodulus_lut and emodulus_lut_provenance (recorded or host) from its @emodulus_lut_json; a file regenerated before #764, or whose attribute is not a record (not an object, no boolean loaded, another provenance), reads both absent as before; a snapshot or annotation that is not a JSON object is reported unreadable, not absent

review_probe.semantics: review_probe_runs(paths): header attributes only (identity, start/end time, counts, run accounting, processing core version), no images or metadata rows; each count and time is read on its own: a missing or unreadable count is null and a recorded 0 stays 0, while a recorded 0 time is null (not recorded); one result per path in order; a file that cannot be read is a per-file error (ok false, message), never a failure of the call; refused as a whole above max_paths or while a review job runs; each file is read under the review session's own lock (HDF5 is not thread-safe, #722) and the open file is left as it was

review_track_rows.semantics: fetch_review_track_rows(valid, track_id, max): the records of the valid or invalid set whose track_id equals track_id (the linked records of one cell), in set order, at most max rows (max above max_rows is refused); positions are their indices in the set, parallel to rows; total counts every match and truncated says total > rows; served from the metadata read at open under the review session's lock, no HDF5 read; refused (ok false, message) for a negative track_id, a raw recording or no open file

review_reprocess_record.semantics: review_reprocess_record(valid, index, settings): the record's stored row next to what the review session's processing kernel finds in the same stored image now; never written anywhere. settings recorded = the file's recorded config, ROI and background (the defaults, said in settings_label, when the file records no config); default = the default config, the whole image, no background. core_version / core_source name the kernel that reprocessed it: the bundled core on a processing instance of the call's own (refused when the review session's active core is another), so no job's instance is touched. pixel_to_micron is the factor it ran and reports with (recorded: the file's, or the fallback when it records none; default: the processing default), named in settings_label; E-LUT (review ABI 4, #764): E (and an E-gated target group) is recomputed with the run's own E-LUT, the table whose bytes have the sha256 its run snapshot v3 emodulus_lut records (a regenerated file: its /experiment_info @emodulus_lut_json with provenance recorded), found among the session kernel's loaded LUT and the bundled LUT, never another; emodulus_lut names it (lut id, revision, the hash's first 12 hex digits) and emodulus_lut_sha256 is its full hash, also named in settings_label. A run that records loaded false gets no E, as it had none; a file without that record (no snapshot, or one before v3), or whose @emodulus_lut_json names only a host's LUT (provenance host), keeps the behaviour before ABI 4 (E not recomputed, settings_label says what the file records). emodulus_recomputed is false in both cases, emodulus_lut and emodulus_lut_sha256 are then empty over the review bridge and null in the shell's JSON, and the reprocessed rows' E is not recomputed (E null). reprocessed holds the objects found (an image with none gives no rows), at most max_objects (truncated), with the record's frame index and no track; match_index (has_match) is the reprocessed object whose centroid, in image coordinates, is nearest the stored one inside the stored bounding box, the stored box and centroid placed in image coordinates through the file's review_object_coordinates; reprocessed rows are image coordinates, stored as stored; object_count_differs when the kernel found another number of objects than a stored object_count above 0. The inputs are read under the job lanes' lock and the review session's lock (HDF5 is not thread-safe, #722); processing runs outside every lock. Refused (ok false, message) while a review job runs, for a raw recording, an index outside the set, a record without a stored image, a file whose object coordinate space is unknown, a run whose recorded E-LUT has no hash or is not available here (the reason names it), an unknown settings value, or when the kernel fails on the image

review_run_statistics.semantics: Review ABI 6 (#716 A7a, building on review ABI 5, #783): review_run_statistics(request_json) -> the JSON document of bridge-contract.json run_quick_look (request, reply, run, statistics and delta exactly as there), computed by the same C++ function (backend::review::computeRunStatistics) for B2 R2's per-run numbers. Each file is read with a short-lived reader of its own under the review session's lock (HDF5 is not thread-safe, #722), gated on the job lanes: while a review job runs every uncached file is deferred, never an error. There is no cache here (computed_at "on_demand", from_cache false) and no instrument, so nothing else defers it. Paths are used as given (no storage root). A read: nothing is written to a file, a store or a snapshot.

review_object_coordinates.semantics: fetch_review_info.object_coordinates (review ABI 3, #756 review 2): the space of the open file's stored bounding boxes and centroids, decided once at open under the review session's lock, in this order: (attribute) /experiment_info @object_coordinates, written from #756 on by the capture path (roi_local for the inline realtime path with an ROI, image otherwise; not written for PL-science runs) and by regenerate / reanalysis (image); (snapshot) a run snapshot v3 of a host-science run: an ROI with w, h > 0 under realtime_mode inline is roi_local, async_batch or no ROI image, another mode does not decide; (roi_origin) an ROI without area or at origin (0, 0): image, both placements being the same; (mask_check) up to max_records records with a mask and a box, the valid set spread over first and the invalid set only to fill the rest: a record votes for the placement of its stored box (as stored, or shifted by the ROI origin) where the stored object is, by identity, not by pixel count: an 8-connected mask component overlapping the placed box whose bounding box has an IoU of at least min_box_iou_percent with it and, where the record has an area, whose measured contour's convex-hull area is within area_tolerance_percent of it (a hole of the component for a Contract 1 inner-contour object, which also needs a hole; its outline otherwise); a record is decisive only when exactly one placement fits, and the file is that space with at least min_decisive decisive votes agreeing at min_agreement_percent or more; otherwise unknown (source empty). object_origin_x / object_origin_y place a stored box or centroid in image coordinates (the ROI origin for roi_local, 0 otherwise). Unknown for a raw recording (no objects) and no open file. Whatever needs the placement (the reprocess match, a cell crop) refuses an unknown space; it never guesses

frame_packet.base: bridge-contract.json frame_packet: the same magic, version, header layout, byte order and limits
frame_packet.identity_semantics: capture_session and store_generation are zero: review frames come from a recorded file, not a capture
frame_packet.rgb8_semantics: review pulls (kinds 3, 5, 6) may carry RGB8 (3 bytes per pixel, stride = width*3) when the backend composed an overlay or ROI; mono pulls are unchanged
frame_packet.thumbnail_strip_semantics: pull kind 5 packs count tiles of size x size as one frame of width size and height size*count; frame_index = page offset

review_density.ramp_semantics: backend/processing/MonitoringDensity.h densityRampColor: linear interpolation over the stops, t in [0,1]; level k of n uses t = k/(n-1) (kdeLevelColor)

review_population.semantics: review_analyze_population(request): expectedPath, feature (area in px², deformability dimensionless or youngsModulus in kPa; review ABI 10 added youngsModulus), nullable inclusive minimum/maximum. Review ABI 10 (#808 F-1): the whole stored file is evaluated natively by the columnar evaluator: the measurement columns are read from /valid_frames/metadata then /invalid_frames/metadata in bounded chunks (Hdf5Service::readMetadataColumns, chunk_events per read), the population graph is evaluated chunk by chunk with unchanged tri-state semantics, and every population's exact membership is held natively as a two-bit-per-event bitset keyed to the source identity and graph revision (membershipKey; reused for the same source and graph: cached true). Only bounded results cross the bridge: counts, statistics, a population table, optional bins and decimated scatter, a page of event references and a 12-image gallery. No implicit validity QC. Refuse raw recording, unreadable metadata, count mismatch, job lane busy or an exceeded resource bound (the reply names it); never sampling. Local evaluation keys (snapshot, unique per call) plus set/decimal ordinal; sourceFingerprint null unless fingerprint true (then the streamed full-file SHA-256, any file size); durable false. Absent fields and nonfinite measurements produce unknown membership; youngsModulus <= 0 is missing; detailed per-event missing reasons are not exposed. No source writes.

bounds.semantics: chunk_events: events per HDF5 read and per evaluation step; max_membership_bytes: all population bitsets of one evaluation (2 bits x events x populations); max_exact_values: selected values held for exact order statistics (8 bytes each). Exceeding a bound refuses with its value; nothing is truncated or approximated.

review_population.statistics: selected, excluded, unknown, measured, missing (decimal strings); minimum, maximum, mean, median, p05, p25, p75, p95, sampleStandardDeviation, cvPercent, geometricMean (null when unavailable): exact, over every selected finite value (estimators: Hyndman-Fan type 7 quantiles, n-1 SD, CV 100*SD/|mean|), the same function (reduceMeasuredValues) as the keyed and F-source paths
review_population.populations: populations: one entry per graph node in topological order {id, parent, selected, excluded, unknown, parentSelected (decimal strings), percentParent (null for an empty parent)}; without a graph the top-level interval is the one population 'interval'
review_population.rows: review ABI 10: rows is a bounded page of event references {key, set, ordinal, membership} of the output population, not every event: optional page {offset, limit (0..page_max_events, default page_default_events), membership all (default) | selected | excluded | unknown}; rowsOffset, rowsLimit, rowsMembership and rowsTotal (decimal string: events matching the filter) describe it
review_population.optional_histogram: histogram {minimum, maximum, bins 1..histogram_max_bins, optional feature (default: the reduction feature)} -> histogram {feature, unit, edges, counts (decimal strings), underflow, overflow, measured, missing}: exact counts of the output population's selected finite values, [left,right) with the last bin closed; sum(counts)+underflow+overflow = measured
review_population.optional_scatter: scatter {x, y, maxPoints 1..scatter_max_points} -> scatter {x, y, eligible, stride, decimated, points [{key, set, ordinal, x, y}]}: every stride-th selected event with both values finite, in event order (deterministic decimation); display only, never used for counts or statistics
review_population.columnar_handle: review ABI 10, additive (#808 F-1b): columnar true (with snapshot semantics) returns {ok, source} where source is the F-source/2 columnar handle of the open stored file (no rows; see analysis_workspace.source); snapshot true alone still returns F-source/1 rows under the rows bound
review_population.evaluation: evaluation {engine native-columnar/1, events, chunkEvents, chunksRead, largestChunk, membershipBytes, bounds}: evidence of the bounded read

optional_graph.semantics: Optional graph replaces the top-level interval membership; top-level feature still selects the reduction. The one native graph compiler (PopulationGates, shared with F-source evaluation) validates fields, geometry, parents/operands/cycles and 256 nodes; features area, deformability, youngsModulus. Interval nodes have id,parent,kind,feature,minimum,maximum; polygon x,y,vertices (3..128, simple); ellipse x,y,centerX,centerY,radiusX,radiusY; quadrant x,y,thresholdX,thresholdY,quadrant; Boolean nodes id,parent,kind,operands (review ABI 10 added the geometry kinds). Recipes are not verified source-bound workspaces.

optional_gallery.request: galleryOffset: unsigned integer, offset among selected observations (review ABI 10: no 10000 cap; past the end is an empty page)
optional_gallery.semantics: gallery entries retain exact snapshot key, set and decimal ordinal. pixels is a 4096-element grayscale byte array or null for unavailable image. Images are copied under the same session lock as evaluation, located through the native membership bitset (rank lookup), not a re-sent row list. Valid-set then invalid-set row order.

analysis_workspace.actions: snapshot, exact read, history, evaluate, gallery, jobInput, report, manifest, method, compare, comparisonSpec, concentrationFit (read); save, restore, import, retainSource, saveFinding (write)
analysis_workspace.comparison_fits: Review ABI 10, additive (#808 F-4: F09, I09, I10; the unmerged ABI 10 contract gains read actions and an optional field, nothing renumbered or removed). comparisonSpec {spec: F-comparison-spec/1 {schema, metric {population, parameter, statistic (mean, median, p05, p25, p75, p95, geometricMean, sampleStandardDeviation, cvPercent), unit}, design unpaired|paired (pairing by experimentalUnit id), groups (2..16, first is the reference), inference none|parametric|rank|both, optional minimumUnitsPerGroup (>= 3, default 3), optional confidenceLevel (default 0.95), samples [{sampleId, group, experimentalUnit, planId, revision (pinned), source}]}} -> {status, comparison: F-comparison/2, contentHash}. Each sample is evaluated through evaluate with the optional metric {population, parameter} field (the pinned revision's population and the named parameter, exact statistics; the reply adds sourceParameters and sourceProvenance). Compatibility against the first sample with a finite metric, with reasons per excluded source: different parameters or units, parameter preprocessing fingerprint, provenance identity (processing core/contract, calibration, E-LUT), missing metric (refused evaluation or no finite statistic), repeated source fingerprint. Groups: n units, unit values (sources sharing a unit within a group are technical replicates averaged), mean, median, SD of unit values. Inference only when declared and every group has >= minimumUnitsPerGroup units (paired: complete pairs), else status insufficient with reasons and no test or p-value: 2 groups unpaired Welch t (CI of the mean difference, Hedges g) and Mann-Whitney U (exact when untied and n <= 50, else normal approximation with tie and continuity correction; Hodges-Lehmann shift, rank-biserial); paired t (CI, dz) and Wilcoxon signed-rank (zeros dropped; exact when untied and n <= 50, else normal approximation with tie correction); > 2 groups one-way ANOVA (eta squared) and Kruskal-Wallis (epsilon squared); paired > 2 groups unsupported. concentrationFit {spec: F-fit-spec/1 {schema, metric, model 4PL|3PL (hill 1), concentrationUnit, concentrationScale log10|linear, weighting none|inverse-variance (1/variance of replicate units per concentration), design independent-units, optional confidenceLevel, samples [{sampleId, experimentalUnit, concentration {value, unit}, planId, revision, source}]}} -> {status, fit: F-fit/1, contentHash}: status fit|insufficient (no parameters, reasons), Levenberg-Marquardt, parameters with SE and CI, EC50 with CI, residuals, R squared, suspect + suspectReasons (not converged, EC50 outside the tested range, EC50 CI wider than the tested range, fewer than 5 concentrations, parameter at bound, singular covariance). Concentrations in another unit or <= 0 are excluded, never converted. Results carry each sample's planId, revision, graphFingerprint and sourceFingerprint.
analysis_workspace.authority: host app.sqlite3 workspace_revisions and workspace_commands; immutable source-bound CAS, exact retry receipts
analysis_workspace.source: stored full-file SHA256, streamed at any file size (review ABI 10; was <=64MiB); live-run/live-epoch fenced E leases; run-archive E-run-events/1; #808 F-1b (additive, review ABI 10): a stored file resolves to an F-source/2 columnar handle (descriptor with schema, storage columnar, sourceKey/fingerprint = full-file SHA-256, scope stored, path, parameters, segments [{set, count}], events, retention file-pinned; no rows). The host lends its chunked columns (RecordingColumns) under the review session lock after re-verifying the fingerprint; the open file uses the session reader, any other path (a retained file-pinned handle) a short-lived reader. evaluate/report/plot/gallery/overlay/compare run on the full file and return bounded results (no per-event rows; membershipStorage native-bitset). observations and jobInput materialize F-source/1 rows under the rows bound (observations: <= 65536 events, 4 MiB).; #808 F-2 (additive): source {kind: fcs, path[, applyGain]} imports an FCS 3.0/3.1 list-mode file through the native reader (FcsReader) as an F-source/2 handle (scope fcs, full-file SHA-256, one segment 'events', explicit per-parameter units, import block with keywords and unsupported constructs: compensation, $PnCALIBRATION, $PnD, $TIMESTEP, extra data sets, ANALYSIS segment, unapplied $PnG); FCS2.0, histogram mode, ASCII, packed or mixed-byte-order data are refused

limits.rows_semantics: F-source/1 carries every event as a JSON row: bounded at rows (review ABI 10; was 10000) with an explicit refusal; larger recordings are analysed by review_population's columnar evaluator. The 64 MiB stored-file cap is removed (streamed SHA-256).

analysis_workspace.method: exact method_id/revision_id/content_hash lookup only; never apply; unavailable/unknown remain explicit
